title: W4 camera-contract elevations are stale at the committed pads: pucks render 60.8° (house 61.4° is actually steepest), docs still claim pucks ≈65° steepest
evidence:
tools/gen_sprites.py:190-192 (build_camera docstring): "atan(9.9 / (0.35 + 4.5*pad)) — pad 0.95 (pucks) => ~65deg STEEP (nearest
top-down); pad 1.95 (campus) => ~47deg SHALLOW". tools/gen_sprites.py:114-115: "# EXCEPTION folded in stage-2: puck pad 0.95 -> 1.15 — at 0.95 the tier_8/16"; :125: "\"puck_1\":   (\"puck\",  1.15, \"tier_4\",  None),". assets/blender/README.md:46: "pucks ≈65° STEEPEST / nearest top-down, campus ≈47° SHALLOWEST". docs/silhouette-spec.md:40: "pucks ≈65° STEEPEST (nearest top-down), campus ≈47° SHALLOWEST". Measured in Blender 5.2 from the committed SPRITE_SPECS pads: house 61.43°, puck 60.83°, host/small_biz 59.85°, dc 52.67°, campus 47.33°.
detail: The docstring's own formula at the committed puck pad 1.15 gives atan(9.9/5.525)=60.8°, not 65°; 65° is the pre-W5-guard pad 0.95. House (pad 1.12, 61.4°) is steepest, so "pucks STEEPEST" and the "~47–65°" range are wrong; build_camera's "pad 0.95 (pucks)" contradicts SPRITE_SPECS in the same file.
recommended_fix: Re-measure and restate the contract from the committed pads (~47–61°; house steepest, campus shallowest) in the docstring, README, and spec §0; drop the stale pad-0.95 example.

title: House colorway recolor silently skips missing material slots — a deleted/renamed contract slot ships mixed-colorway sprites with no fold-in gate firing
evidence:
tools/gen_sprites.py:249-252: "for slot, factor in SHADE_LADDER.items():
                m = bpy.data.materials.get("%s_%s" % (family, slot))
                if m is not None:
                    emission_set(m, hex_rgba(colorway, factor))". tools/gen_sprites.py:99: "\"fill_hip\": 0.94,       # host cap's -X facet (reads the hip edge)". assets/blender/README.md house contract row: "`house_fill`, `house_fill_roofshade`, `house_fill_lit`, `house_fill_mid`, `house_fill_shade` — all recolored per colorway through the sun ladder".
detail: The silent skip is structurally required for absent-by-design slots (house has no fill_hip), so a missing-by-accident slot is indistinguishable: house_1..3 render with a stale coral tone on that face while the bbox guard (alpha-only) stays green — violating the file's own fail-loudly contract and project 'never catch-and-ignore'.
recommended_fix: When colorway is set, assert the family's full README-contract slot list resolves (all 5 house slots); SystemExit on a missing one, mirroring emission_set/hex_rgba.

title: test_sprite_order.py negative self-test never exercises the comparator — vacuous against its stated purpose (#79 r2 W4 claim)
evidence:
tools/test_sprite_order.py:65-70: "# negative self-test: the comparator must BITE on a drifted order (a
    # comparator regression must never pass CI unflagged — #79 r2 W4)
    mutated = list(of)
    mutated[-1], mutated[-2] = mutated[-2], mutated[-1]  # the r1 swap itself
    if mutated == of:
        print("FAIL: negative self-test — mutation did not drift (broken test)")" — mutated is never compared against so/jo or any comparison logic.
detail: The leg only proves a 2-swap changes a Python list; a comparator regression (e.g. 'if so != of and jo != of' dropping the json-leg drift, or a dropped check entirely) still passes CI green, contradicting the docstring's 'the comparator must BITE on a mutated order'.
recommended_fix: Extract the triple comparison into a helper main() calls (e.g. orders_consistent(so, of, jo)); assert in the test that it returns False for the mutated order.

title: Puck tier solo only traverses direct child collections — nested or scene-root objects render into every puck and pass the W5 bbox guard
detail: Objects linked directly to sc.collection, or tier collections nested one level deeper, are never hidden: all tiers render into every puck. The combined bbox is non-empty and interior (tier_16 clears by ≥13px at pad 1.15), so only a later T2 pixel mismatch catches it.
recommended_fix: When soloing, also set hide_render on sc.collection.objects and walk collection children recursively (or assert exactly tier_4/8/16 sit at the top level).
